title: Sisters sue Española over traffic stop they say was illegal

reports.title: Sisters sue Española over traffic stop they say was illegal

summary:
Two Rio Arriba County sisters are suing Española over a July 23 traffic stop they say was illegal. Jaclynn Gonzales, 21, was driving with her 12-year-old sister when a Flock Safety camera misread their plate, reading a final 2 as 7 and flagging the car as stolen from Rio Rancho. Officers stopped them, handcuffed both, and placed them in separate police cars before noticing the error. Jaclynn asked police to call their nearby mother to pick up the girl, but officers instead handcuffed the child and put her in another vehicle.

The sisters filed separate lawsuits on January 3 seeking unspecified damages for anxiety, fear, worry, and restricted movement. Their attorney, Sheri Raphaelson, filed a similar case in April for Adam Pacheco, then 17, who was forced to kneel after being wrongly linked to an armed robbery. The city, Police Chief Mizel A. Garcia, and Flock Safety did not respond to requests for comment. No next court date is mentioned.
